1. Approach and rationale

1.1 Central idea

The primary strategy is a hybrid construction-and-polish method. It is intentionally different from the previous parent program in that it does not start by polishing the supplied solution as the main job. Instead, it first builds many valid, diverse, smaller grid solutions—most importantly balanced discrete binary sequences—because the exact evaluator is cheap on small grids and binary sequences often lift to strong continuous designs. Every constructed sequence is strictly evaluated with the evaluator, not with a surrogate. After a valid candidate is discovered at a grid length, the construction is transferred to a short-to-medium set of grid lengths and polished with a dedicated constrained minimax local procedure.

The hybrid has three coherent stages:

- Stage A: exact binary discovery by simulated annealing and randomized transition-on-occurrence, on even grid lengths from about 24 to 80. This stage deliberately explores non-parent basins. It maintains the exact mass n/2 on integer grids by using swaps between one 1 and one 0, so feasibility is structural and never delegated to project-only repair at the center.
- Stage B: optional mixed-integer discovery, for small even n, if a CVXPY mixed-integer solver is available. This stage is an accelerator and may be skipped instantly if unavailable or if time is short. It gives rigorous upper-bound models only for the exact binary model and has no effect on the final continuous candidate unless an independently evaluated candidate is produced.
